claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and the considered equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Removing one or more elements from the quinary alloy changes short-range order.
Removing one or more elements from the quinary alloy changes local lattice distortions.
Short-range order affects dislocation mobility in these FCC alloys.
Local lattice distortions affect dislocation mobility in these FCC alloys.
Short-range order and local lattice distortions alter the operative deformation mechanisms.
Differences in short-range order and local lattice distortions explain differences in mechanical properties among the quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys.
At room temperature under uniaxial tensile loading, the quinary alloy will have higher strength than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
At room temperature under uniaxial tensile loading, the quinary alloy will have lower ductility than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
The quaternary and ternary subsets will exhibit composition-dependent variations in strength and ductility.
The proposed mechanism applies under the boundary condition of single-phase FCC microstructures without precipitates or other secondary phases.
A controlled tensile comparison can test whether mechanical-property variations correlate with short-range order and local lattice distortion.
